messages.content: What is the best way to extract the unique elements from an array and return them sorted in ascending order? For a list of numbers 3 1 2 1 4 3

function.name: getUniqueSorted
function.description: This function takes an array of elements and returns a new array of unique elements sorted in ascending order. It does not require any additional parameters for sorting. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

array.description: The array from which to extract unique elements and sort them. This is JavaScript array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type integer; they are not in string representation.

message.content:
### Quick answer

```js
const arr = [3, 1, 2, 1, 4, 3];
const uniqueSorted = [...new Set(arr)].sort((a, b) => a - b);
console.log(uniqueSorted);   // → [1, 2, 3, 4]
```

---

## Why this works

| Step | What happens | Why it’s good |
|------|--------------|---------------|
| `new Set(arr)` | Creates a `Set` that automatically removes duplicates. | `Set` keeps only one copy of each value. |
| `[...new Set(arr)]` | Turns the `Set` back into an array. | We need an array to sort. |
| `.sort((a, b) => a - b)` | Sorts numerically in ascending order. | The default `Array.prototype.sort()` sorts strings lexicographically, so we supply a numeric comparator. |

**Time complexity:**  
- Building the `Set`: **O(n)**  
- Converting to an array: **O(n)**  
- Sorting: **O(n log n)**  

Overall: **O(n log n)**, which is optimal for sorting.

---

## Using the provided helper (`getUniqueSorted`)

If you’re working in an environment where the helper function is available, you can simply call it:

```js
// The helper expects a *string* representation of the array
const result = getUniqueSorted({ array: "[3,1,2,1,4,3]" });
console.log(result);   // → [1, 2, 3, 4]
```

> **Note:** The helper internally does the same thing as the manual snippet above.

---

## Alternative: Using `Array.from` (ES6)

```js
const uniqueSorted = Array.from(new Set(arr)).sort((a, b) => a - b);
```

`Array.from` is just another way to convert a `Set` back into an array.

---

## If you need to keep the original array untouched

The code above never mutates `arr`. It creates a new array (`uniqueSorted`) that contains the unique, sorted values.

---

## Full example (Node.js / browser)

```js
// Input array
const numbers = [3, 1, 2, 1, 4, 3];

// 1. Remove duplicates
const unique = [...new Set(numbers)];

// 2. Sort ascending
const sortedUnique = unique.sort((a, b) => a - b);

console.log(sortedUnique); // [1, 2, 3, 4]
```

You can drop this snippet into any JavaScript runtime (Node, browser console, etc.) and it will give you the desired result.
